qs.q: A 60-year-old woman receiving prolonged broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy develops severe oral thrush. Scrapings examined in potassium hydroxide show budding yeast cells and pseudohyphae. Which virulence factor is primarily responsible for the transition of this organism from commensal to invasive pathogen?
o: Acquisition of foreign antibiotic resistance plasmids via bacterial conjugation
Secretion of potent exotoxins that lyse host mucosal epithelial cells
Phenotypic switching facilitating adherence and transition to hyphal forms
Production of thick gelatinous capsules preventing any complement deposition
Formation of environmentally resistant endospores surviving extreme heat
qs.e: Candida albicans undergoes phenotypic switching and yeast-to-hypha transition, enhancing tissue penetration and adherence.

qs.q: A 45-year-old presents with new-onset scaly erythematous plaques on the extensor surfaces. Which condition must be ruled out with potassium hydroxide preparation before confirming this diagnosis?
qs.e: Superficial fungal infections can mimic plaque psoriasis, requiring exclusion via KOH test. Allergic contact dermatitis presents with acute vesiculation rather than chronic scaly extensor plaques.
qs.s: Pathology of Acute Skin Inflammation: Urticaria & Eczema: MCQs

qs.q: In the laboratory diagnosis of dermatophytoses, a clinical specimen of skin scales is treated with 10-20% potassium hydroxide (KOH). What is the primary purpose of adding KOH to the preparation?
o: D. It selectively suppresses saprophytic bacterial growth in culture.
C. It kills live fungal cells while preserving their structure with phenol.
B. It stains fungal glucan and chitin with a bright blue dye.
A. It digests protein debris and keratin, making fungal structures visible.
qs.e: KOH acts to digest protein debris and clear keratin from skin, nail, or hair specimens so that branching hyphae or spores can be visualized clearly. Lactophenol Cotton Blue contains phenol to kill organisms, whereas KOH is solely a clearing agent.
qs.s: Mycoses: Superficial, Cutaneous & Systemic Fungal Infections: MCQs

qs.q: A 22-year-old college student presents with asymptomatic, mildly scaling spots on his upper chest and back that fail to tan when exposed to sunlight. Scrapings examined with potassium hydroxide show short hyphae and clustered yeast cells. What is the most likely physical finding on the skin?
qs.e: Tinea versicolor classically presents with irregular hypopigmented and hyperpigmented macules due to interference with melanin production by Malassezia metabolites. Tinea corporis typically shows annular erythematous plaques with central clearing rather than the fine scale of pityriasis versicolor.
